{{short description|American mathematician|bot=PearBOT 5}}
'''David Clark Dobson''' (born 17 November 1962 in [[Salt Lake City]]) is an American mathematician.

Dobson received in 1986 his bachelor's degree from [[Utah State University]] and his PhD in 1990 from [[Rice University]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=39351}}</ref> He was at the [[University of Minnesota]] from 1990 to 1993. He was from 1993 to 1996 an assistant professor, from 1996 to 2000 an assistant Professor and from 1996 to 2000 an associate professor at [[Texas A&M University]]. Since 2002 he is a full professor at the [[University of Utah]].<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=David C. Dobson, C.V.|website=Mathematics Department, University of Utah|url=http://www.math.utah.edu/~dobson/bio.html}}</ref>

Dobson does research on [[applied mathematics]], specifically, "computational methods and optimal design for [[plasmonic]] structures and [[metamaterial]]s, optimal design of photonic structures and devices, data analysis with physical constraints, and [[inverse problems]] in acoustics."<ref name=Research>{{cite web|title=David C. Dobson, Current Research|website=Mathematics Department, University of Utah|url=http://www.math.utah.edu/~dobson/research.html}}</ref>

In 2000 he received the first [[European Mathematical Society|Felix Klein Prize]]. From 1997 to 1999 he was a Sloan Fellow.<ref name=CV/>
